## CT 1: quadratic_x_intercepts_ct_001

- Type: MCQ
- Difficulty: MEDIUM
- Total variants: 2

### Variant 1

#### Question

The graph of \(y = x^2 - 4\) is shown below.
![Upward parabola with vertex at (0, -4) crossing the x-axis at -2 and 2](https://example.com/assets/parabola_x2_minus_4.png)
Select all values of \(x\) at which the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis.

#### Options

- [x] \(x = -2\)
- [x] \(x = 2\)
- [ ] \(x = 4\)
- [ ] \(x = -4\)

#### Solution

The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis where \(y = 0\):
\[
x^2 - 4 = 0 \implies (x - 2)(x + 2) = 0
\]
So \(x = 2\) or \(x = -2\). The value \(-4\) is the \(y\)-intercept, and \(x = 4\) gives \(y = 12\), so neither is an \(x\)-intercept.

#### Hint

Set \(y = 0\) and factor the difference of squares.

### Variant 2

#### Question

The graph of \(y = x^2 - 9\) is shown below.
![Upward parabola with vertex at (0, -9) crossing the x-axis at -3 and 3](https://example.com/assets/parabola_x2_minus_9.png)
Select all values of \(x\) at which the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis.

#### Options

- [x] \(x = 3\)
- [ ] \(x = -9\)
- [x] \(x = -3\)
- [ ] \(x = 9\)

#### Solution

The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis where \(y = 0\):
\[
x^2 - 9 = 0 \implies (x - 3)(x + 3) = 0
\]
So \(x = 3\) or \(x = -3\). The value \(-9\) is the \(y\)-intercept, and \(x = 9\) gives \(y = 72\), so neither is an \(x\)-intercept.

#### Hint

Set \(y = 0\) and factor the difference of squares.

## CT 2: odd_even_proofs_ct_002

- Type: OPEN_ENDED
- Difficulty: MEDIUM
- Total variants: 2

### Variant 1

#### Question

Explain why the sum of two odd integers is always even.

#### Solution

Write the odd integers as \(2m + 1\) and \(2n + 1\) for integers \(m\) and \(n\). Their sum is \(2m + 2n + 2 = 2(m + n + 1)\), which is a multiple of \(2\), so it is even.

#### Hint

Write each odd integer in the form \(2k + 1\).

### Variant 2

#### Question

Explain why the product of two odd integers is always odd.

#### Solution

Write the odd integers as \(2m + 1\) and \(2n + 1\). Their product is \(4mn + 2m + 2n + 1 = 2(2mn + m + n) + 1\), which is one more than a multiple of \(2\), so it is odd.

#### Hint

Write each odd integer in the form \(2k + 1\) and expand.

## CT 3: polygon_angle_sums_ct_003

- Type: TRUE_FALSE
- Difficulty: EASY
- Total variants: 2

### Variant 1

#### Question

The interior angles of every triangle add up to \(180^\circ\).

#### Answer

True

#### Solution

Drawing a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side creates alternate angles that together form a straight line, so the three angles sum to \(180^\circ\).

#### Hint

Think about a straight line drawn through one vertex.

### Variant 2

#### Question

The interior angles of every quadrilateral add up to \(360^\circ\).

#### Answer

True

#### Solution

A diagonal splits a quadrilateral into two triangles, each with angle sum \(180^\circ\), so the total is \(2 \times 180^\circ = 360^\circ\).

#### Hint

Split the shape into triangles with a diagonal.

## CT 10: rectangle_measurements_ct_010

- Type: OPEN_ENDED_SUBPART
- Difficulty: MEDIUM
- Total variants: 1

### Variant 1

#### Question

The rectangle \(ABCD\) shown below measures \(6\) cm by \(4\) cm.
![Rectangle ABCD, 6 cm long and 4 cm wide, with diagonal AC drawn](https://example.com/assets/rectangle_6_by_4.png)

#### Part 1: OPEN_ENDED

##### Question

Find the area of the rectangle.

##### Solution

Area \(= 6 \times 4 = 24\,\text{cm}^2\).

##### Hint

Multiply the length by the width.

#### Part 2: OPEN_ENDED

##### Question

Find the length of a diagonal of the rectangle.

##### Solution

By Pythagoras, the diagonal is \(\sqrt{6^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{52} = 2\sqrt{13}\,\text{cm}\).

##### Hint

The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.

#### Part 3: OPEN_ENDED

##### Question

Explain why the diagonal is longer than either side.

##### Solution

The diagonal is the hypotenuse of right triangle \(ABC\).
\[
AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 > AB^2
\]
Since \(BC^2 > 0\), \(AC\) is longer than \(AB\), and similarly longer than \(BC\).

##### Hint

Compare the hypotenuse with each leg using Pythagoras.

## CT 11: data_set_statistics_ct_011

- Type: MCQ_SUBPART
- Difficulty: EASY
- Total variants: 1

### Variant 1

#### Question

Consider the data set \(4, 6, 6, 8\).

#### Part 1: MCQ

##### Question

What is the mean of the data set?

##### Options

- [x] \(6\)
- [ ] \(5\)
- [ ] \(7\)
- [ ] \(8\)

##### Solution

The sum is \(4 + 6 + 6 + 8 = 24\), and \(24 \div 4 = 6\).

##### Hint

Add the values and divide by how many there are.

#### Part 2: MCQ

##### Question

What is the mode of the data set?

##### Options

- [x] \(6\)
- [ ] \(4\)
- [ ] \(8\)
- [ ] \(5\)

##### Solution

The value \(6\) appears twice, more often than any other value.

##### Hint

Look for the value that appears most often.

#### Part 3: MCQ

##### Question

Select all statements that are true for this data set.

##### Options

- [x] The median is \(6\)
- [x] The range is \(4\)
- [ ] The mean is \(7\)
- [ ] The mode is \(4\)

##### Solution

The median is the mean of the middle values \(6\) and \(6\), which is \(6\). The range is \(8 - 4 = 4\). The mean is \(6\), not \(7\), and the mode is \(6\), not \(4\).

##### Hint

Compute each statistic before judging the statements.

## CT 14: prime_number_statements_ct_014

- Type: TRUE_FALSE_SUBPART
- Difficulty: MEDIUM
- Total variants: 1

### Variant 1

#### Question

Decide whether each statement about prime numbers is true or false.

#### Part 1: TRUE_FALSE

##### Question

The number \(91\) is a prime number.

##### Answer

False

##### Solution

\(91 = 7 \times 13\), so it has factors other than \(1\) and itself.

##### Hint

Try dividing by small primes.

#### Part 2: TRUE_FALSE

##### Question

The number \(97\) is a prime number.

##### Answer

True

##### Solution

\(97\) is not divisible by \(2\), \(3\), \(5\), or \(7\), and \(11^2 > 97\), so it is prime.

##### Hint

You only need to test primes up to the square root.

#### Part 3: TRUE_FALSE

##### Question

Every even number greater than \(2\) is composite.

##### Answer

True

##### Solution

An even number greater than \(2\) is divisible by \(2\) and by itself, so it has at least three factors.

##### Hint

Consider the factor 2.
